prompt:
以下はある英語ニュースpodcast記事のFull Story・Point One・Point Twoです。
Point One・Point Twoそれぞれについて、以下6項目を判定してください
(それぞれPASS/FAIL)。

- qa_not_caveat_only: このPointが、研究上の限界・一般化上の注意・免責事項
  だけで構成されていない場合PASS(それらに加えて実質的な新しい内容がある
  場合もPASS。留保だけでPoint枠全体が終わっている場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_full_story_paraphrase: Full Storyの要約・言い換えに留まっていない
  場合PASS(Full Storyの中心的なlogic・結論を語彙だけ変えて繰り返している
  場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_other_point_paraphrase: もう一方のPointの要約・言い換えになって
  いない場合PASS
- qa_explains_why_it_matters: 「だから何なのか」を具体的に説明できている
  場合PASS(聞き手にとっての具体的な意味・示唆がある場合)
- qa_specific_not_generic: この記事のLedger固有の内容に基づいており、他の
  どんな記事にもほぼそのまま流用できる一般論になっていない場合PASS
- qa_adds_new_value: 新しい理解・解釈・意外性・具体的示唆のいずれかを
  実際に加えている場合PASS(Full Storyだけを聞いた場合と比べて、聞き手の
  理解が実際に深まっている場合)

reasoningには、判定理由を1〜2文の日本語で書いてください(特にFAILの場合は
具体的な理由を明記してください)。

【Full Story】
A new report in the New England Journal of Medicine describes a different way to make CAR-T cells: inside the patient’s body.

The paper appeared online in early September 2026 and in the journal’s September issue. It reports a phase 1 study of 16 people with hard-to-treat neurological autoimmune diseases. The group included patients with progressive multiple sclerosis, MOG antibody-related disease, generalized myasthenia gravis, and idiopathic inflammatory muscle disease.

Each patient received one dose through a vein. The treatment used a gene carrier designed not to reproduce itself. It delivered the CAR gene to the patients’ own T cells. Inside the body, those cells became CD19 CAR-T cells, which are designed to target B cells.

This is different from taking cells out of the body, changing them in a laboratory, and then putting them back.

After treatment, B cells fell deeply and later began to return. Across the four disease groups, researchers reported improvements in nerve function, symptoms, scores, or blood tests.

Researchers also watched safety closely. Eleven of the 16 patients developed grade 1 cytokine release syndrome, an immune reaction that included short-term fever in some cases. It appeared between days 5 and 28, and all cases eased within two weeks. The study reported no immune-related nerve toxicity, low blood pressure, or low oxygen.

But this was a small, early study with one treatment group and no control group. The results are signals to study further, not final proof that the treatment works.

【Point One】
The striking biological detail is that B cells did not stay gone. They fell deeply in the blood, bone marrow, and the fluid around the brain and spinal cord, then began to return at a median of about two months. That makes this look more like a temporary reset of the B-cell system than permanent removal. Future studies will need to ask whether benefits last as B cells return, and whether another dose is needed.

【Point Two】
The four disorders should not be read as one shared result. Researchers used different yardsticks: nerve function and scans in one group, antibodies in another, and scores or muscle blood markers elsewhere. The groups were also small—seven people in one disease group and three in each of the others. With no control group, the next test must ask, disease by disease, what changed beyond changes that might happen without treatment.

point_one.reasoning: 血液だけでなく骨髄や脳脊髄液でもB細胞が減少後に中央値約2か月で戻ったという具体的情報を示し、治療が恒久的除去ではなく一時的な免疫リセットかもしれないと解釈している。効果の持続性や再投与の必要性という、Full Storyだけでは得にくい実質的な示唆を加えている。

point_two.reasoning: 4疾患で評価指標が異なり、患者数も1群7人・他群各3人だったことを具体化し、全疾患に共通する効果として扱えない理由を説明している。無対照試験の限界を単に繰り返すのではなく、疾患ごとに自然経過を超える変化を検証すべきだという解釈を加えている。
